Hi Anna — thanks for the note and great seeing SkyForge on the demo.

Attached is a short pack with three proposal templates and a worked ramp worksheet (see attachments). Quick summary up front:

- Option A "Lean Floor": 16 GPUs committed (min), support for 2x burst capacity for short periods. Best for teams that want low upfront cost and are comfortable with occasional soft-fallback to on-demand.
- Option B "Balanced Slate": 32 GPUs committed with 25% burst window. Recommended if you have predictable peak windows (inference + nightly embedding ops).
- Option C "Anchored Slate": 48 GPUs committed with contractual warm-standby and 4-week notice for scale changes (SLA-backed).

Key ramp examples included (in the spreadsheet):
- 3-month quick ramp (16 -> 32): short onboarding, higher burst reliance.
- 6-month steady ramp (16 -> 32 -> 32): phased activation to smooth burn.
- 12-month staged (16 -> 24 -> 32 -> 48): conservative onboarding with capacity triggers.

I've CC'd Karthik from Capacity Planning — he'll add a note on minimum pod sizing and activation windows if you want to keep the floor lower or build a geo-burst plan.

Deliverables attached: SkyForge_Rsv_Options_v1.pdf, Reserved_Ramp_Template.xlsx

Next steps: tell me which option looks closest to what procurement prefers and we'll put a draft statement of work and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Anna — quick technical note on the minimum footprint and activation cadence.

Operational constraints we typically advise (short version):
- Minimum activation unit is a 4-GPU pod for our scheduler (for A100-class); fractional allocations inside a pod are not supported.
- Warm-up period: multi-node KV cache seeding and model warmup typically takes 30–90 minutes depending on model seq length distribution. Plan for a 2 hour SLA window to reach steady-state for large models.
- Burst model: we can support temporary burst to on-demand fleet for up to 48 hours without reconfiguring the reserved slate; beyond that we recommend a warm-start tranche.

Practical guidance: If your steady QPS maps to ~12 GPUs, a 16-GPU floor gives 25% headroom and aligns to our 4-GPU pod units. If you expect growth >2x in three months, consider the 32-GPU balanced slate to avoid frequent ramp triggers.

I've added Marissa (Sales Engineering) for runbook language and to capture any compliance/contract asks. Happy to hop on a quick 30-minute call to translate QPS to GPU maps if helpful.

—Karthik

- Geo-burst: we can route the nightly embedding window to a West-US on-demand pool (costed as on-demand) with an automated fallback to reserved nodes if warm-start tranches are present. Shortest warm-start notice we support for adding a tranche is 14 days (operational prep + kernel tuning).
